local.h: Senators seek probe of Folkston ICE center
local.b: After another detainee death, Sens. Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff asked DHS to investigate whether officers retaliated against hunger strikers at the South Georgia facility, including placing at least 13 in solitary confinement.
local.title: Another death at Georgia ICE facility as hunger continues

goodnews.b: Music fans are rallying to support Dean Schlabowske of the Waco Brothers, who faces six-figure medical costs after an acute myeloid leukemia diagnosis.

local.h: Walter Koenig, Star Trek's Chekov, dies at 90
local.b: Koenig, who played Ensign Chekov on the original 'Star Trek' series and several movies, died Monday at his home in North Hollywood, his agent said.
local.title: Walter Koenig, Ensign Chekov on original 'Star Trek' series, dies at 90

local.h: LA speed cameras begin issuing warnings
local.b: Twenty-six of the city's 125 speed cameras are now live, issuing warnings for 60 days before fines start at $50 for going 11 mph over the limit.
local.title: Start watching your speed, LA speed cameras go online today

local.h: Pressure grows on Mamdani over specialized schools
local.b: Former schools chancellor David Banks, Public Advocate Jumaane Williams and three borough presidents are expected to call Tuesday for admissions reform at the city's specialized high schools.
local.title: Pressure grows on Mamdani to reform admissions to NYC specialized high schools

local.h: Council to weigh juvenile jail changes
local.b: The NYC Council will consider changes to juvenile detention as assaults and overcrowding rise. A mother says her son was attacked by other teens while held at Horizon in the Bronx.
local.title: NYC Council to weigh changes to juvenile jails as assaults and overcrowding rise

local.h: NYers face higher health costs as enrollment opens
local.b: New Yorkers without employer coverage can shop for 2027 plans on the state marketplace starting Nov. 1, and many will feel the effects of federal health spending cuts, including reduced eligibility for the Essential Plan.
local.title: What NYers can expect as open enrollment for health insurance begins

local.h: Judge halts overnight work at Chinatown jail site
local.b: A Manhattan Supreme Court judge temporarily halted after-hours construction on the new Chinatown jail after residents sued over sleep disruption, another setback for the city's plan to replace Rikers Island.
local.title: Judge temporarily halts overnight construction at NYC’s Chinatown jail

goodnews.h: Rockefeller tree is a 76-foot upstate spruce
goodnews.b: The Norway spruce from West Edmeston will be cut Nov. 5, arrive Nov. 7 and be lit Dec. 2 with more than 50,000 LED lights and a Swarovski star.
goodnews.title: Rockefeller Center's 2026 Christmas tree is a 76-foot spruce from Upstate New York

goodnews.h: East Brooklyn NYCHA homes get $636M upgrade
goodnews.b: Nearly 3,000 residents of the Reid & Park Rock developments now live in renovated apartments with new kitchens, bathrooms and modernized heating and ventilation, NYCHA said.
goodnews.title: In East Brooklyn, aging NYCHA homes get a $636M upgrade

local.h: Protesters plan Halloween sit-ins in France
local.b: Organisers of 'Act III - Halloween' plan sit-ins outside town halls and the Assemblée Nationale on Oct. 31, though no demonstrations have yet been declared to Paris police.
local.title: Protests in France: What to expect on October 31st

local.h: Paris extends summer café terraces a month
local.b: Summer terraces can stay until the end of November instead of coming down Oct. 31, at no extra charge, to support cafés, bars and restaurants hit by protest violence on Oct. 17 and 18.
local.title: Paris extends summer café terraces for another month

local.h: French rail unions join November 5 strike
local.b: Four main rail unions will join Thursday, Nov. 5's cross-sector strike over the draft 2027 budget, wages, jobs and public services.
local.title: French rail workers join November strike

local.h: Lecornu, ministers to meet student leaders
local.b: Prime Minister Lecornu and education ministers Edouard Geffray and Philippe Baptiste meet student leaders Monday at Matignon after another weekend of protests over lycée conditions and the cost of living.
local.title: France's PM and key ministers to meet student leaders on Monday

local.h: Seattle schools weigh merging at least 6 schools
local.b: Families at Orca K-8, Martin Luther King Jr., Sacajawea, John Rogers, View Ridge and Decatur were emailed Oct. 23 about proposed mergers for the 2027-28 school year, two years after a plan to close four schools died.
local.title: Seattle Public Schools weighs mergers for at least 6 schools

local.h: Council moves to restore fire overtime
local.b: Seattle City Council members are coordinating to restore about $7 million in Seattle Fire Department overtime that Mayor Wilson proposed cutting, among a flood of budget adds.

local.h: DOJ asks Washington to set aside 400 ballots
local.b: The Justice Department asked the state to hold ballots from 400 people it says may be noncitizens until their eligibility is confirmed. Secretary of State Steve Hobbs is reviewing the demand.
local.title: Trump administration asks Washington state to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens

local.h: Microsoft offers buyouts to a quarter of workforce
local.b: The Redmond company is offering voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees at the vice president level and below, comparable to its standard severance, as it further reduces headcount.

local.h: Loggers say Roadless Rule repeal won't fix woes
local.b: With the 25-year-old rule's formal repeal expected early next year, people who make a living in the forests say their problems are bigger than forest access, starting with record-high diesel prices.
